claim: The CLIP text encoders truncate the prompt at 77 tokens, and do so silently with no error returned
what_it_does_not_establish: What a token is in words. The tokenizer is subword, so a word count is an estimate and a long brand name can cost several tokens on its own
how_to_use_it: This is the only documented reason front-loading a prompt is real. On a CLIP-only pipeline everything past the window is not weighted less, it is absent

claim: SD3 and SD3.5 carry a T5-XXL encoder alongside CLIP and the model card states a 256-token sequence length
what_it_does_not_establish: That the CLIP branch also reads 256. The 77-token CLIP window still applies to the CLIP embeddings inside the same model
how_to_use_it: Treat 256 as the T5 budget and 77 as the CLIP one. A prompt between the two is read by one encoder and cut by the other

claim: Removing the T5-XXL encoder costs a 38 percent win rate on written text specifically, and much less on general prompt following
what_it_does_not_establish: That the same holds for any other model family. This is one ablation on one architecture
how_to_use_it: The one published number connecting an encoder to a capability. Cite it when somebody claims typography quality is a prompt-wording problem

claim: The SD3 paper contains no 77-versus-256 token ablation; those sequence-length figures come from the SD3.5 model card, not the paper
what_it_does_not_establish: Anything about what the numbers mean, only where they are not
how_to_use_it: Correction. Cite the model card for the numbers and the paper for the encoder ablation, never the paper for both

claim: No token limit is documented for any Imagen version. The widely repeated 128-token figure belongs to Parti, a different Google model
what_it_does_not_establish: That Imagen has no limit. It establishes only that no published limit exists
how_to_use_it: Correction. If a prompt has to be sized for Imagen, size it by testing, not by the 128 figure

claim: The prompt maximum is 32000 characters for the GPT image models, 4000 for dall-e-3 and 1000 for dall-e-2
what_it_does_not_establish: A token limit, or where the model stops paying attention. It is an API validation limit in characters, which is a different kind of constraint from an encoder window
how_to_use_it: Correction to this row's first version, which recorded no published limit after reading only the guide page. The number is on the API reference, not the guide. 32000 characters is far past any useful prompt, so treat it as a validation ceiling rather than a budget to fill

claim: No prompt token or character limit is published
what_it_does_not_establish: That length has no effect
how_to_use_it: Same as OpenAI: measure rather than cite a number somebody posted

claim: negativePrompt is supported on imagen-3.0-generate-001 and capability-001 and is documented as a legacy feature not included from imagen-3.0-generate-002 onward
what_it_does_not_establish: Behaviour on Gemini image models, which are a different surface
how_to_use_it: Check the exact model string before sending the field. Between two Imagen 3 point releases the same request is valid and then silently unsupported

claim: No negative-prompt parameter. The docs instead list semantic negative prompts as a prompting practice, meaning exclusions written in natural language
what_it_does_not_establish: That natural-language exclusion works as well as a dedicated field
how_to_use_it: Write the exclusion as a positive description of what should be there instead. An empty street, not no people

claim: No negative-prompt parameter exists in the image generation documentation
what_it_does_not_establish: That exclusions cannot be expressed, only that there is no field for them
how_to_use_it: Never emit a negative-prompt block for this family. It is not ignored politely, it is read as part of the prompt

claim: FLUX.2 does not support negative prompts, and the prompting guide says to describe desired outcomes rather than exclusions
what_it_does_not_establish: Behaviour of FLUX.1 open-weight checkpoints run through a local pipeline, which do expose the field
how_to_use_it: The gate that matters most in this skill: a compiled FLUX prompt carrying a DO NOT list is sending the exclusions as content

claim: A Negative Prompt setting exists and guides generation away from specified content, with the regular prompt always favoured over it
what_it_does_not_establish: How strongly it weights, which is not published
how_to_use_it: Write nouns and attributes, never negated sentences, and never contradict the positive prompt

claim: Negative prompts are not restricted on turbo models; sd3.5-large-turbo and sd3.5-flash differ from non-turbo in the cfg_scale default of 1 versus 4
what_it_does_not_establish: That a negative prompt is equally effective at cfg_scale 1, which is the real caveat
how_to_use_it: Correction to the common claim that turbo models drop negatives. Raise guidance before concluding the field does nothing

claim: negativePrompt is live on v3 images generate-async and fill-async, unsupported with Custom Models on Image Model 3 and 4, and absent from the v4 and Image Model 5 schema
what_it_does_not_establish: That the field was removed from Firefly generally, which is the usual overstatement
how_to_use_it: Route by endpoint version, not by product name. The same account has both behaviours available

claim: Text in an image is documented with a 25-character guideline and up to three short phrases
what_it_does_not_establish: A word count, and anything about Gemini image models. Google publishes characters, not words, and only for Imagen
how_to_use_it: The only published numeric text budget in the whole survey. Use it as the design constraint for any generated headline and set longer copy in layout

claim: In-image text is listed under Limitations: the model can still struggle with precise text placement and clarity
what_it_does_not_establish: A failure rate. No benchmark figure is published
how_to_use_it: Quote this to a client before promising rendered packaging or legal copy. The vendor calls it a limitation, so the risk is not a matter of prompt skill

claim: Documented techniques: put the exact string in quotation marks with intended capitalization and name font, size, colour and placement; spell uncommon names letter-by-letter; ask for sharp text rendering when the layout is dense
what_it_does_not_establish: That any of the three raises accuracy by a measured amount
how_to_use_it: Apply all three and still inspect every character. They reduce the failure rate, they do not remove the inspection step

claim: Text must be inside double quotation marks; single quotes and apostrophes do not trigger text generation. Works best with the Latin alphabet and short phrases
what_it_does_not_establish: Any character limit or accuracy figure
how_to_use_it: The only provider documenting a required syntax rather than a style. Vietnamese diacritics fall outside the documented alphabet, so treat them as untested

claim: Documented recovery when text fails: switch to Raw mode or lower stylize. Text generation is documented as a V6-and-later feature
what_it_does_not_establish: That stylize is the cause rather than a correlate
how_to_use_it: Change one of the two, regenerate, and record which one moved it, so the finding survives the session

claim: Text Effects is a separately defined feature and Adobe IP indemnification covers output generated from 13 September 2023 onward, expressly not extending to the letter and character shapes themselves
what_it_does_not_establish: Indemnity for any other provider, and cover for the typeface design itself
how_to_use_it: The commercially load-bearing line for typography work. Generated letterforms are not covered, so licensed type still has to be set in a design tool

claim: No in-image text guidance located for FLUX.1 or FLUX.2. The overview page returned a content-filter block on two attempts and was not characterised from memory
what_it_does_not_establish: Anything about FLUX text quality in either direction
how_to_use_it: Recorded as a hole rather than filled with a plausible sentence. Reopen this row when the page is reachable

claim: The cref and cw parameters are V6-only, oref and ow are V7-only, neither functions in the current default V8.2, and cref has been removed from the Parameter List page entirely
what_it_does_not_establish: What replaces them in V8.2, which is not documented
how_to_use_it: Correction, and the most consequential one here. Every character-consistency tutorial in circulation teaches a parameter that no longer runs on the default model

claim: Every provider that documents character consistency documents it as reference-image conditioning, none as prompt wording, and each states it is not guaranteed
what_it_does_not_establish: A similarity metric or a pass rate for any provider
how_to_use_it: Why this skill locks identity in a parameter sheet and a seed rather than in adjectives. Wording is not a documented consistency mechanism anywhere

claim: Seeds produce similar but not identical results on current Midjourney models
what_it_does_not_establish: Which model versions were identical, if any
how_to_use_it: Never promise a client an identical regeneration from a stored seed here. Store the output file, because the seed is not a substitute for it

claim: The seed and addWatermark parameters are mutually exclusive
what_it_does_not_establish: Whether the watermark or the seed is the better thing to keep
how_to_use_it: A real fork: on Vertex you get reproducibility or the default SynthID watermark, not both. Decide it at pipeline design time, not per run

claim: No seed parameter is documented for the image models, and seed language is absent from both the DALL-E 3 and the 4o system cards
what_it_does_not_establish: That output is not reproducible by some other route
how_to_use_it: Reproducibility on this family comes from keeping the prompt and the file, not from a parameter

claim: DALL-E 2 and DALL-E 3 are deprecated and removed from the API. Current models are gpt-image-2 flagship, gpt-image-1.5, gpt-image-1 and gpt-image-1-mini
what_it_does_not_establish: That DALL-E behaviour documented in its system card describes the current models. It does not
how_to_use_it: Anything in this skill naming DALL-E as the OpenAI image API is out of date. The system-card findings still apply historically, not operationally

claim: All Imagen models are deprecated with shutdowns beginning 30 June 2026 and 17 August 2026, in favour of Gemini image models
what_it_does_not_establish: Which Gemini model is the like-for-like replacement for a given Imagen call
how_to_use_it: A published expiry date on anything built on Imagen. Both dates sit on or before a 2026-07-31 run, so verify the endpoint responds before quoting the capability

claim: The text encoder used by Imagen 3, Imagen 4 or any Gemini image model has never been disclosed. T5-XXL is documented only for the 2022 research model
what_it_does_not_establish: The encoder for any current Google image model
how_to_use_it: Correction to the common claim that Imagen uses T5-XXL today. Without the encoder you cannot reason about a token window, which is consistent with none being published

claim: Text rendering is not discussed in the Imagen 3 technical report at all; the paper contains no occurrence of text render or typograph
what_it_does_not_establish: That the capability is absent, only that the paper does not address it
how_to_use_it: Keeps the 25-character guideline attached to the prompt guide rather than to the paper, which says nothing on the subject

claim: The Vertex REST reference, the edit-images page and the customize pages were removed, and generate-images now contains no occurrence of sampleCount, sampleImageSize, outputOptions or storageUri
what_it_does_not_establish: That the parameters stopped working, only that they stopped being documented
how_to_use_it: Do not reconstruct wire parameter names from memory for this family. Read them off a live successful request or do not send them

claim: 4o image generation permits generating adult public figures with an opt-out mechanism, while DALL-E 3 blocked them and provided no opt-out
what_it_does_not_establish: The publicity, personality or moral rights that apply in Vietnam or anywhere else. A model permission is not a legal permission
how_to_use_it: Read as vendor policy only. The rights question for a real person is answered in claims-proof-ledger.md, not in a system card

claim: Fewer than 2.6 percent of alpha images, about 3500 of more than 100000, contained public figures
what_it_does_not_establish: How often the attempt was made, only how often it appeared in the sample
how_to_use_it: Useful as scale context for a policy conversation. Not a benchmark of anything about your own prompts

claim: C2PA metadata is attached to all 4o image assets; DALL-E 3 carried none
what_it_does_not_establish: That the metadata survives a platform upload, which strips it routinely
how_to_use_it: Assume disclosure is machine-readable at the point of generation and gone by the time it is posted. Disclose in the caption if disclosure matters

claim: Prompt transformation is described as a policy step in the DALL-E 3 system card and is absent from the 4o addendum
what_it_does_not_establish: What the current models do with a submitted prompt
how_to_use_it: Explains why a prompt and its result diverged on DALL-E 3. Do not carry the explanation forward to gpt-image without evidence

claim: No system card exists for gpt-image-1, 1.5 or 2, verified against the 34 sub-sitemaps of the openai.com sitemap and the safety index
what_it_does_not_establish: The safety or policy behaviour of the current image models
how_to_use_it: The current flagship image model ships without the document people cite for it. Anything attributed to a gpt-image system card is invented

claim: Commercial questions of likeness, ownership and indemnity resolve in licence and contract text rather than model documentation, and three of the four major providers gate indemnity behind a revenue threshold or an enterprise agreement
what_it_does_not_establish: The terms of any specific account, which is the only version that binds
how_to_use_it: Read the plan the client is actually on. Indemnity present in a marketing page is frequently absent from the tier they pay for

claim: The midjourney.com legal terms-of-service path and the adobe.com firefly-user-guidelines path both return 404; the live terms are the Zendesk article and the Adobe Gen AI User Guidelines
what_it_does_not_establish: What changed in the terms when the page moved
how_to_use_it: Cite the URL that resolves today. A dead legal URL in a client deck reads as though the terms were never checked

claim: Used through the Responses API image tool, the mainline model automatically revises the prompt for improved performance
what_it_does_not_establish: What it changes, or whether the revision is returned to you
how_to_use_it: The prompt you wrote is not necessarily the prompt that ran. Call the images endpoint directly when the wording is the thing under test, or a one-variable iteration is measuring two changes

claim: Imagen on Vertex exposes ENABLE_PROMPT_REWRITING, an LLM-based rewriting feature, and its default value is true
what_it_does_not_establish: What the rewriter does to a specific prompt
how_to_use_it: Set it false before any prompt A/B, or the comparison is between two rewrites rather than two prompts. The doc warns that disabling it may reduce quality, which is the trade

claim: Documented prompt-structure guidance: for complex scenes with many elements, break the prompt into steps
what_it_does_not_establish: Any ordering or position effect. It is a structure recommendation, not a weighting rule
how_to_use_it: The only prompt-structure instruction any of these providers publishes. Note what it is not: it says nothing about putting important words first

claim: No guidance on prompt structure or clause ordering appears on the image generation guide; its headings run Overview, Generate Images, Edit Images, Customize Image Output, Limitations, Content Moderation, Cost and latency
what_it_does_not_establish: That ordering has no effect
how_to_use_it: Every ordering rule circulating for this family is inferred, not documented. Say so when handing over a prompt template

claim: Listed under Limitations: the model may occasionally struggle to maintain visual consistency for recurring characters or brand elements across multiple generations
what_it_does_not_establish: A failure rate, or which of character and brand element fails more often
how_to_use_it: The vendor names recurring-character drift as a limitation of the current flagship. Quote it before promising a brand mascot across a campaign, and budget for the retries

claim: Listed under Limitations: the model may have difficulty placing elements precisely in structured or layout-sensitive compositions
what_it_does_not_establish: Which layouts fail. No examples are given
how_to_use_it: Generate the scene, then place logo, headline and legal copy in layout. This row is the vendor agreeing with that division of labour

claim: Documented input limits: gemini-2.5-flash-image works best with up to 3 input images, gemini-3-pro-image supports 5 at high fidelity and up to 14 in total, and gemini-3.1-flash-image supports character resemblance for up to 4 characters and fidelity for up to 10 objects in one workflow
what_it_does_not_establish: How closely a resemblance holds, which is not quantified anywhere
how_to_use_it: The only published numbers for a character-consistency mechanism in this whole table. Four characters is the documented ceiling for a group shot with recurring people, so a five-person cast needs compositing

claim: The model will not always follow the exact number of image outputs requested
what_it_does_not_establish: How often it deviates
how_to_use_it: Count the returned assets in the pipeline rather than assuming n. A batch script that assumes the requested count will silently produce short sets

claim: Documented text guidance: Gemini works best if you first generate the text and then ask for an image containing it
what_it_does_not_establish: A character budget or an accuracy figure
how_to_use_it: Two calls, not one: settle the copy, then render it. Which is also how the copy gets reviewed before it is inside a JPEG

claim: gpt-image-2 accepts any resolution satisfying four constraints: maximum edge at most 3840px, both edges multiples of 16px, long-to-short edge ratio at most 3:1, and total pixels between 655360 and 8294400
what_it_does_not_establish: Anything about earlier models, which are restricted to a fixed size list
how_to_use_it: The multiple-of-16 rule is the one that bites: a 1080x1920 story frame is legal, a 1000x1500 one is not. Check the channel spec against these four before building a size list

claim: Outputs above 2560x1440, about 3686400 pixels, are described as experimental
what_it_does_not_establish: What experimental means for reliability or price
how_to_use_it: Generate at or below 2K and upscale in the finishing step, rather than asking the model for print resolution

claim: gpt-image-2 does not support transparent backgrounds, and requests with background transparent are not supported for this model
what_it_does_not_establish: Whether earlier gpt-image models still accept it
how_to_use_it: A packshot needing a cutout cannot be generated transparent on the flagship. Plan a masking step, or route that one asset to a model that supports it

claim: Documented aspect ratios are 1:1 default, 3:4, 4:3, 16:9 and 9:16
what_it_does_not_establish: Arbitrary ratios, which are not offered
how_to_use_it: Five ratios, so any other frame is a crop decided by you rather than the model. Decide it against composition-grids.csv, not by centring

claim: gemini-3.1-flash-image documents fourteen aspect ratios including 1:1, 2:3, 3:2, 3:4, 4:3, 4:5, 5:4, 9:16, 16:9, 21:9 and the extremes 1:4, 4:1, 1:8 and 8:1
what_it_does_not_establish: Quality at the extreme ratios
how_to_use_it: 8:1 and 1:8 exist for banner and skyscraper slots that otherwise get cropped out of a square. Check the channel spec first, because most placements do not accept them

claim: SEED_NUMBER is any non-negative integer in the range 1 to 2147483647, and providing the same seed number always results in the same output images
what_it_does_not_establish: Determinism across model versions, or with prompt rewriting enabled
how_to_use_it: The strongest reproducibility language any provider publishes, and the reason plan_virtual_person.py emits a seed inside this range. It is also the row that collides with the watermark

claim: No seed parameter is documented for the Gemini API image models; the word seed does not appear on the page, which documents output format, aspect ratio and image size only
what_it_does_not_establish: That output cannot be pinned some other way
how_to_use_it: Any claim that a Nano Banana model takes a seed has no primary source. Reproducibility here means keeping the reference images and the file

claim: Images generated with ChatGPT, Codex and the API include both C2PA metadata and SynthID watermarks, and SynthID embeds a signal in the image itself that may persist through some edits
what_it_does_not_establish: Which edits it survives, and whether it can be removed
how_to_use_it: Supersedes the 4o system-card row for current models: provenance is no longer only metadata that an upload strips. Assume an AI-generated asset is detectable and disclose deliberately rather than by accident

claim: All generated images include a SynthID watermark
what_it_does_not_establish: Whether it can be removed or disabled. The page states it is applied and says nothing either way about removal
how_to_use_it: Not optional on this surface, so there is no watermark-versus-seed trade to make here - there is no seed either

claim: The watermark is added automatically and cannot be disabled from the Google Cloud console; through the API addWatermark defaults to true and must be set false explicitly, and a watermarked image carries a verifiable SynthID
what_it_does_not_establish: Whether disabling it is permitted by the terms, which is a separate question from whether the API allows it
how_to_use_it: The console and the API differ, which is worth knowing before somebody concludes the watermark is mandatory from clicking around. Turning it off to get a seed is a decision to record, not a default

claim: The Terms of Use state that as between you and OpenAI you own the Output, and OpenAI assigns to you all its right, title and interest in it; the help centre adds that OpenAI will not claim copyright over content generated by the API
what_it_does_not_establish: Whether the output is copyrightable at all, or whether it infringes anything. An assignment of whatever rights the provider holds is not a warranty that rights exist
how_to_use_it: The clearest ownership language of any provider here. Quote it to a client asking who owns the asset, and pair it with the separate point that ownership and indemnity are different questions

claim: No ownership-of-generated-output or commercial-use clause was found across the Google Terms of Service, the Generative AI Additional Terms, the generative AI use policy or the Gemini API image documentation. The Terms clause that your content remains yours is scoped to content you upload, submit, store, send, receive or share, not to model output
what_it_does_not_establish: That you do not own the output. It establishes that Google does not say so where you would look
how_to_use_it: The asymmetry to know before choosing a provider for client work: one of the two writes down who owns the image and the other does not. Do not paraphrase the uploaded-content clause as an output-ownership clause

claim: The Generative AI Additional Terms of Service state they no longer apply as of 22 May 2024 unless you are a business partner with a signed agreement referencing them, because the main Terms were updated to cover AI topics
what_it_does_not_establish: What moved into the main Terms and what was dropped
how_to_use_it: Anything cited from that page is quoting a retired document. Cite the main Terms, and check the signed agreement if there is one

claim: Prohibited conduct includes using AI-generated content from the services to develop machine learning models or related AI technology
what_it_does_not_establish: Whether ordinary campaign use is affected. It is not; this is about training
how_to_use_it: Relevant the moment somebody proposes fine-tuning a house model on generated assets. That specific plan is prohibited by the terms of the service that produced them

claim: The usage policies prohibit use of someone's likeness, including their photorealistic image or voice, without their consent in ways that could confuse authenticity, listed under a privacy heading
what_it_does_not_establish: The publicity or personality rights that apply in any given country, which are stricter in several
how_to_use_it: This is the operative rule for current models, not the 4o system card. Note the qualifier: it is scoped to confusing authenticity, and local law is not

claim: The generative AI use policy prohibits violating the rights of others including privacy and intellectual property, gives using personal data or biometrics without legally-required consent as its example, and separately prohibits impersonating an individual living or dead without explicit disclosure in order to deceive
what_it_does_not_establish: Whether a stylised likeness counts as impersonation
how_to_use_it: The word biometrics is doing work here: a face is biometric data, so a real-face reference is a consent question before it is a craft question

claim: The use policy prohibits misrepresenting the provenance of generated content by claiming it was created solely by a human in order to deceive, and the main Terms list misleading others into thinking generative AI content was created by a human as prohibited conduct
what_it_does_not_establish: What disclosure wording satisfies it
how_to_use_it: Both pages make undisclosed AI authorship a terms question, not only an ethics one. Which settles the recurring argument about whether a generated campaign image needs disclosure

claim: PERSON_SETTING controls face and person generation with three values: allow_all including minors, the default for Imagen 4 generation models and imagen-3.0-capability-001; allow_adult for adults only including celebrities, the default for all other models; and dont_allow
what_it_does_not_establish: How the classifier decides, or its error rate
how_to_use_it: Set it explicitly rather than inheriting a default that differs by model. allow_adult permitting celebrities is a provider permission and not a rights permission

claim: No person_generation parameter appears in the Gemini API image documentation
what_it_does_not_establish: What the surface does about people, only that it exposes no control
how_to_use_it: Do not port the Vertex parameter across. A request carrying it is being sent to an endpoint that does not document it

claim: Grounding with Google Search does not support using real-world images of people from web search on gemini-3.1-flash-image at this time
what_it_does_not_establish: Behaviour on other models in the family
how_to_use_it: The one path that would have pulled a real face in from the web is closed on this model, which is the outcome this skill wanted anyway

claim: Moderation strictness is a parameter: auto applies standard filtering that seeks to limit certain categories of potentially age-inappropriate content, and low is less restrictive filtering
what_it_does_not_establish: What moves between the two settings
how_to_use_it: Leaving it at auto is a choice with consequences for false refusals on beauty and swimwear work. Record which setting produced a delivered asset

claim: The Vertex generative AI image pages carry a banner that Vertex AI documentation is no longer being updated and that its services are now part of the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, and the negative-prompt page recommends updating model endpoints before 30 June 2026
what_it_does_not_establish: Whether the documented behaviour still holds. A frozen page describes the past accurately and the present only by luck
how_to_use_it: Every Vertex-sourced row in this table is a fact about Imagen-on-Vertex, not about the current Gemini API surface. Do not carry seed, watermark, negative-prompt or personGeneration behaviour across the boundary
